title: Metabolic labeling and LC-MS/MS-based identification of interleukin-1α-induced secreted proteomes from epithelial cells in the presence or absence of serum
protocol: Trypsinize HCT116 from a confluent dish and seed 5 × 10^6 cells in new 145 mm cell culture dishes with 20 mL complete medium.
Carefully wash cells three times in 10 mL warm DPBS to remove serum and methionine present in the medium.

Cultivate cells in 10 mL methionine-free DMEM with no (0%) or 1% FBS, adding additional supplements of 6 mM L-glutamine, 0.5 mM L-cysteine, 20 μg/mL streptomycin, and 20 U/mL penicillin to all samples.
Add recombinant IL-1α (10 ng/mL) directly to the medium for half of the cells.
In parallel to IL-1α stimulation, add 25 μM L-HPG or 25 μM L-methionine as a control, respectively, directly to the medium.
Incubate cells in a humid atmosphere at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for further 6 hours.
Collect supernatants and transfer to 15 mL tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 3000 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer clear supernatant to new tubes or freeze at -80°C.
Optional: Harvest cells by washing with ice-cold PBS twice, then scraping in PBS.
Centrifuge cell suspension at 500 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatants and store the cell pellet at -80°C.
Transfer supernatants to a new 50 mL tube.
Slowly add 40 mL of ice-cold acetone (-20°C) to 10 mL of supernatant using a glass pipette.
Incubate at -20°C for 16-22 hours.
Centrifuge at 15,000 × g at 4°C for 15 minutes, remove acetone.
Add 2 mL cold (4°C) methanol to the precipitate, vortex.
Transfer sample to a new 2 mL reaction tube and centrifuge at 15,000 × g at 4°C for 15 minutes to further remove acetone.
Repeat step to wash the precipitated protein pellet two times.
Discard methanol and dry pellet at 18-22°C for 5 minutes.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL CLICK chemistry lysis buffer containing 100 mM HEPES at pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 1% Nonidet P-40, 2 mM PMSF and 1× complete EDTA-free protease inhibitor mixture (Roche).
Prepare the reagent mix for the CLICK reaction.
Add 160 μL of the reagent mix to the sample.
Incubate the mixture for 1.5 hours at 18°C–22°C with slow rotation on an Intellimixer RM-2 or a similar rotating device.
Transfer the CLICK conjugate to 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Slowly add 4 mL of cold acetone (−20°C) to 1 mL of CLICK conjugate.
Incubate at −20°C for 16–20 hours.
Centrifuge the mixture at 15,000 × g at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Remove the supernatant.
Add 2 mL cold (4°C) methanol to the precipitate.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly.
Transfer the mixture to a new 2 mL reaction tube.
Centrifuge the mixture again at 15,000 × g / 4°C for 15 minutes.
Remove acetone.
Repeat step b to wash the precipitated protein pellet 2×.
Discard methanol and dry protein pellet at 18°C–22°C for 5 minutes.
Resuspend pellet in 60 μL of 1% Nonidet P-40, 0.1% SDS in PBS (washing buffer I) at 18°C–22°C.
Pause point: Samples can be stored at −80°C for several days.
Optional: Pass precipitated proteins lysed in 120 μL of PBS containing 1% SDS through a 0.5 mL Zeba spin desalting column with a 7 kDa cutoff to remove CLICK reagents and free biotin-azide.
Resuspend the settled Pierce™ streptavidin magnetic beads by vortexing.
Transfer 30 μL for Western blotting and 40 μL for mass spectrometry of each sample into separate 1.5 mL reaction tubes using a cut-off 200 μL tip.
Remove storage buffer using a magnetic device.
Wait for 1 minute until beads stick to the magnet.
Equilibrate or wash the beads two times with washing buffer I containing 500 μL of 1% Nonidet P-40, 0.1% SDS in PBS at 4°C with slow rotation (22 rpm) on an Intellimixer or similar rotating device.
Remove buffer using the magnetic device.
Add 25 μL (for Western Blot) or 35 μL (for mass spectrometry) of supernatant proteins solubilized in 1% Nonidet P-40, 0.1% SDS in PBS to the beads.
Incubate for 16–22 hours at 4°C with slow rotation on an Intellimixer RM-2 device or a similar rotating device.
Purify biotinylated proteins by washing magnetic beads sequentially using slow rotation on an Intellimixer RM-2 device (program F1, 22 rpm) at 4°C.
Remove washing buffers using a magnet after each wash.
Wash twice with 500 μL PBS including 1% Nonidet P-40, 0.1% SDS (washing buffer I) for 10 minutes.
Wash three times with 500 μL ice-cold PBS including 6 M Urea (washing buffer II) for 10 minutes.
Incubate samples for 10 min.
Wash samples three times with 500 μL ice-cold PBS for 10 min each time.
For Western blotting, add 30 μL 2× RotiLoad buffer and boil beads at 95°C for 20 min.
Transfer supernatants to new reaction tubes and discard beads.
For nanoHPLC-MS/MS, add 60 μL of MS-buffer (20 mM Tris-HCl pH 8.0, 2 mM CaCl2) and transfer samples at 4°C to the mass spectrometry lab for on-bead trypsin digestion.
Prepare a 12.5% separating gel.
Overlay separating gel with 70% isopropanol and incubate for at least 20 min.
Remove isopropanol and prepare a 5% stacking gel with a silicon comb inserted.
Incubate the stacking gel for 10 min.
Remove the comb and fill chamber with 1× Laemmlie buffer.
Load 30 μL supernatants from beads into individual lanes of one gel.
Run the gel at 50 mA for 2.5 hours.
Cut four filter papers (Whatman) of required size for each gel.
Soak two filter papers in 1 × Western blot buffer.
Cut the membrane (Roti-PVDF [Roth]) based on gel-size and activate it in pure methanol for approximately 3 minutes.
Equilibrate the membrane in 1 × Western blot-buffer together with the two filters.
Place the separating-gel on top of the stack (observe correct orientation).
Allow the stack to equilibrate shortly before placing it on the bottom (+ pole) of the blotting-chamber.
Place two more filter papers soaked in Western blot buffer on top of the membrane-gel stack.
Put the lid (- pole) carefully on top and close the screws gently.
Run the blot setup at 101 mA for 2 hours (0.8 mA / cm²).
Flush the membrane with desalted water to remove gel- and filter-fragments after blotting.
Block the membrane for 16–22 hours with 5% BSA in TBS-T.
Metabolically label HCT116 cells cultured in methionine-free DMEM without or with FBS using L-HPG.
Stimulate cells with 10 ng/mL IL-1α for 6 hours before metabolic labeling.
Purify supernatant proteins on streptavidin beads.
Perform CLICK reactions in vitro to biotinate precipitated proteins from supernatants.
Analyze aliquots of supernatant proteins by SDS-PAGE and Western blotting.
Visualize the biotinylated fraction using streptavidin horseradish peroxidase conjugates.
Incubate membrane with streptavidin-HRP conjugates at a 1:5000 dilution in 5% BSA in TBS-T.
Wash membrane four times with TBS-T for 5 minutes each.
Develop blot using ECL detection reagents by incubating the membrane in ECL reagent for 1–2 minutes.
Remove ECL reagent and wrap the membrane in clear film.
Measure ECL signals using the ChemiDoc instrument or a similar device.
Stain membrane in Coomassie solution for approximately 10 minutes.
Destain membrane with Coomassie destaining solution three times for 10 minutes each.
Dry membrane and take a picture.
Remove buffer from streptavidin magnetic beads.
Add 0.1 μg trypsin solubilized in 50 μL of MS-buffer to each sample.
Incubate for 45 min at 37°C.
Transfer supernatant to fresh tubes using the magnetic separator to precipitate the beads.
Continue incubation of the supernatant at 37°C for 16–22 h.
Add DTT to a final concentration of 5 mM to the tryptic peptide solution.
Mix the sample and incubate for 15 min at 95°C.
Add iodoacetamide to a final concentration of 25 mM.
Mix the sample thoroughly.
Incubate the mixture for 45 minutes at 18°C–22°C in the dark.
Add DTT to a final concentration of 50 mM.
Mix the sample thoroughly.
Incubate the mixture for 1 hour at 18°C–22°C.
Add 150 μL acetonitrile onto the column.
Place the column in a 2 mL tube and centrifuge for 30 seconds at 300–400 × g.
Discard the flowthrough.
Add 150 μL double distilled H2O / 0.1% TFA onto the column.
Place the column in a 2 mL tube and centrifuge for 30 seconds at 300–400 × g.
Discard the flowthrough.
Repeat steps iv.–vi. three times in total.
Pipette the peptide solution on the column.
Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 300–400 × g.
Discard the flowthrough.
Add 150 μL of 5% acetonitrile / 0.1% TFA onto the column.
Centrifuge for 2 minutes at 300–400 × g.
Discard the flowthrough.
Repeat steps iii. and iv. three times in total.
Place the column in a fresh 2 mL tube.
Add 150 μL 50% acetonitrile / 0.1% TFA and centrifuge for 1 min at 300–400 × g.
Repeat step ii and combine eluates.
Concentrate and dry peptides in a vacuum concentrator.
Solubilize and dilute peptides.
Resuspend peptides in 25 μL LC-MS/MS loading buffer.
Measure peptide concentrations using a Nanodrop™ device at the OD of 280 nm.
Place samples in the autosampler of the mass spectrometer.
Choose suitable separation and data-acquisition methods depending on the equipment used.
Use a column temperature of 50°C on a nanoElute nanoHPLC-system equipped with a 25 cm Aurora column.
Run a linear increase from 2% to 17% solvent B within 60 min.
Follow with a linear gradient up to 25% solvent B within the next 30 min.
Increase to 37% solvent B for an additional 10 min.
Increase solvent B to 95% within 10 min and hold for an additional 10 min.
Use a flow rate of 400 nL/min with water / 0.1% formic acid (solvent A) and acetonitrile / 0.1% formic acid (solvent B).
